title: Fire radiative power and energy
text: FRP is instantaneous fire radiative power in MW, equivalent to MJ per second. FRE is energy integrated over time in MJ. One GJ is 1000 MJ. Summing instantaneous satellite FRP samples does not give energy. The local scientific energy tool integrates calibrated daily FRE over the cube cells represented each day. Estimates depend on temporal reconstruction and sensor coverage.

title: Satellite detections and incident identity
text: NASA FIRMS detections are satellite thermal anomalies, not a count of distinct fires. A single fire may generate many detections over different sensors and days. Thermal anomalies can also be agricultural burning or industrial sources. A selected polygon or H3 hexagon is a query area, not a confirmed wildfire perimeter. Zero detections do not prove absence of fire: clouds, overpasses, thresholds and archive coverage affect observation.

title: MODIS and VIIRS sensor comparability
text: VIIRS provides 375 m active-fire detection, while the nominal MODIS active-fire product is 1 km. Resolution, sensitivity and overpass differences can alter raw counts. Introducing VIIRS from 2012 is not proof of an increase in actual fire incidents. There is no universal 400 or 420 percent correction. The application uses calibrated FRE rather than raw counts for scientific energy comparisons.

title: Reconstruction and uncertainty
text: RTS Kalman smoothing estimates missing daily thermal measurements using a state model, other available sensors and a historical cross-sensor prior. A reconstructed value is an estimate, not a direct observation or proof of a continuing fire. A 95 percent model interval describes uncertainty of the modeled state; it is not the probability that a named fire occurred. Partially reconstructed days can also contain real observations.

title: Ignition and fire spread evidence
text: Satellite thermal detections alone cannot establish what ignited a fire. Ignition evidence requires a matching investigation or incident report. Wind, high temperature, low humidity and fuel conditions can affect spread but do not establish ignition. A command post location is not necessarily the location of a fire. A regional report is not proof that each selected satellite cell belongs to that incident. A cause absent from retrieved reports is unverified in those reports, not necessarily unknown to authorities.

title: Biomass and emission estimates
text: The application estimates dry biomass consumed using 0.368 kg per MJ of integrated FRE. For GJ this is energy_GJ times 0.368 tonnes. Episode scenario emissions assume 9.5 g PM2.5 per kg biomass and 1580 g CO2 per kg biomass. These constant factors do not establish measured emissions, ambient air concentrations, health impacts, casualties, ecological damage or burned hectares. Emission factors vary with fuel and combustion. Dashboard PM2.5 and burned-area validation fields can remain null.

title: Industrial thermal screening
text: Persistent thermal activity can indicate gas flaring or another industrial heat source. Temporal entropy or an industrial screening flag alone does not identify a facility. Current real-cube industrial scores may remove no cells; report actual counts rather than promising filter effectiveness. Industrial candidates should not automatically be explained using wildfire news.

title: Local archive and map scope
text: The scientific cube covers available Earth observations within 2001–2026; actual date coverage varies by area. Four UI study envelopes are Iberia (Spain and Portugal), Chilecito La Rioja Argentina, Orlando Florida USA, and Amazonas/Manaus Brazil. The Amazonas envelope is not all Amazonia. Selected polygons and dates take priority unless the current question explicitly changes place or time. H3 R7 cells and unique R4 parents filter the database. Scientific totals integrate the daily represented footprint, not the full polygon every day. Synthetic mode is opt-in and cannot verify real incidents.

title: Thermal episode duration
text: The episode profiling tool discovers the greatest daily energy within available history when no date is specified. It computes consecutive above-background activity in a window of 15 days before and after the peak, with robust same-month background from other years. This is a statistical thermal episode that can include several fires. It is not the official ignition, containment or extinction interval. If activity reaches the window or archive edge its duration is censored and may extend beyond the reported interval.
